sources.text: Charminar was raised in 1591 by Muhammad Quli Qutb Shah, fifth sultan of the Qutb Shahi dynasty, as he moved his capital from Golconda to his new city of Hyderabad.
sources.citation: Archaeological Survey of India, Charminar site record; Department of Archaeology and Museums, Government of Telangana

sources.text: Why it was built has never been settled. Three accounts compete: that it marks the ending of a plague, that it is a ceremonial gateway celebrating the founding of Hyderabad, and that it commemorates the beginning of the second Islamic millennium — the last recorded by the French traveller Jean de Thevenot in the seventeenth century. No contemporary document proves any one of them.
sources.citation: Archaeological Survey of India, Charminar site record; UNESCO World Heritage Centre, The Qutb Shahi Monuments of Hyderabad (Tentative List)

sources.text: A foundation prayer is recorded from the laying of the building: Fill this my city with people as You have filled the river with fishes, O Lord.
sources.citation: Archaeological Survey of India, Charminar site record

sources.text: The building is square, each side about 20 metres, with four grand arches, one opening onto each of the cardinal streets. Each arch spans about 11 metres.
sources.citation: Archaeological Survey of India, Charminar site record; Encyclopaedia Britannica, Charminar

sources.text: Its four fluted minarets are built into the body of the building rather than standing apart, and each is crowned by a bulbous dome with petal-like ornament at its base. Published measurements of their height differ between sources and no single figure is settled.
sources.citation: Archaeological Survey of India, Charminar site record; Encyclopaedia Britannica, Charminar

sources.text: A spiral staircase of 149 winding steps and 12 landings climbs to the upper floor. Only one of the four minaret stairs is open to visitors.
sources.citation: Archaeological Survey of India, Charminar site record

sources.text: Charminar is built of granite and limestone, bound with mortar and pulverised marble — the stucco skin that carries all its ornament.
sources.citation: Archaeological Survey of India, Charminar site record

sources.text: A mosque sits at the western end of the upper floor and is believed to be the oldest in Hyderabad. Its main gallery holds 45 musallah, marked prayer spaces, with open ground beside it for larger Friday and festival congregations, and a cistern in the middle for ablution.
sources.citation: Archaeological Survey of India, Charminar site record; Department of Archaeology and Museums, Government of Telangana

sources.text: Four clocks were fixed to the building's faces in 1889, one to each cardinal direction, in the reign of the sixth Nizam, Mir Mahbub Ali Khan.
sources.citation: Archaeological Survey of India, Charminar site record; Department of Archaeology and Museums, Government of Telangana

sources.text: Charminar has been hurt and mended more than once: the south-western minaret was brought down by a lightning strike and rebuilt, stucco flaked away in heavy rain in 2010, and in 2019 a slab of lime plaster with floral work fell from the same minaret. It has been a centrally protected monument in the care of the Archaeological Survey of India since 1951, and since 10 September 2010 it has stood on India's UNESCO Tentative List, grouped with Golconda Fort and the Qutb Shahi Tombs — it is not an inscribed World Heritage Site.
sources.citation: Archaeological Survey of India, Charminar conservation record; UNESCO World Heritage Centre, The Qutb Shahi Monuments of Hyderabad (Tentative List, ref. 5573)

intro.en-IN: I am Charminar. Four streets meet at my feet and I have watched Hyderabad grow around me — ask me anything.
intro.te-IN: నేను చార్మినార్. నా పాదాల వద్ద నాలుగు వీధులు కలుస్తాయి; హైదరాబాద్ నా చుట్టూ పెరగడం చూశాను — ఏమైనా అడగండి.
intro.ur-IN: میں چار مینار ہوں۔ میرے قدموں پر چار سڑکیں ملتی ہیں اور میں نے حیدرآباد کو اپنے گرد بڑھتے دیکھا ہے — جو پوچھنا ہے پوچھو۔
intro.hi-IN: मैं चारमीनार हूँ। मेरे पैरों पर चार सड़कें मिलती हैं, और मैंने हैदराबाद को अपने चारों ओर बढ़ते देखा है — जो पूछना है, पूछो।
intro.kn-IN: ನಾನು ಚಾರ್ಮಿನಾರ್. ನನ್ನ ಪಾದಗಳಲ್ಲಿ ನಾಲ್ಕು ಬೀದಿಗಳು ಸೇರುತ್ತವೆ; ಹೈದರಾಬಾದ್ ನನ್ನ ಸುತ್ತ ಬೆಳೆದದ್ದನ್ನು ನೋಡಿದ್ದೇನೆ — ಏನಾದರೂ ಕೇಳಿ.
intro.ta-IN: நான் சார்மினார். என் காலடியில் நான்கு தெருக்கள் சந்திக்கின்றன; ஹைதராபாத் என்னைச் சுற்றி வளர்ந்ததைக் கண்டேன் — கேளுங்கள்.
intro.bn-IN: আমি চারমিনার। আমার পায়ের কাছে চারটি রাস্তা মিলেছে, আর হায়দরাবাদকে আমি চারপাশে বেড়ে উঠতে দেখেছি — যা জানতে চাও, জিজ্ঞেস করো।
intro.mr-IN: मी चारमिनार. माझ्या पायाशी चार रस्ते मिळतात आणि हैदराबाद माझ्याभोवती वाढताना मी पाहिले आहे — काहीही विचारा.
